parole.significato: A form of oriental ruby, carbuncle or possibly jasper
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Latin chodchod, a transliteration of Hebrew כַּדְכֹּד. parole.significato: A former Hebrew liquid measure of volume (about 3.8 L).
parole.testo: From Middle English hin, from Latin hin, from Hebrew הִין, from Egyptian h:n-nw-w-W22 (hnw, “jar, unit of liquid volume”).

parole.significato: Artifacts, or less commonly, matters pertaining to the Jews, their culture or their religion, particularly ritual objec…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin iūdaica, neuter plural of iūdaicus (“Jewish”), from Hebrew יְהוּדָה (Yehuda, “Judah”). By surface analysis, Juda + -ica. Doublet of giudecca and Judecca.

parole.significato: A very large wine bottle (named after the King) with the capacity of about 18 liters, equivalent to 24 standard bottles.
parole.testo: From Latin Melchior, from Hebrew מלכיאור (“king of light”), from מלך (“king”) + אור (“light”).
From Latin non serviam (“I will not serve”), used in the Vulgate to translate Hebrew לֹא אעבוד.

parole.significato: Honorific epithet used parenthetically to mark a beloved person as being deceased.
parole.testo: A calque of Latin beatae memoriae, possibly a calque of Hebrew זיכרונו לברכה (zikhronó/á/ám/án livrakhá, “memory-of-him/her/them to blessing”), ז״ל (Z.L.).
From Latin paschālis; ultimately from Hebrew פסח (pésakh). Doublet of Pascal and pascal.

parole.significato: One who protested in the Rebecca Riots; a Rebeccaite.
parole.testo: The Vulgate (Latin) form of biblical Rebekah, from Hebrew רִבְקָה (Rivka, “enchantingly beautiful, captivating, snare”).

parole.parola: there is nothing new under the sun
parole.significato: There is nothing truly novel in existence; every new idea has some sort of precedent or echo from the past.
parole.testo: Calque of Latin nihil sub sōle novum, itself a calque from the Hebrew אֵין כָּל חָדָשׁ תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ (en kol chadásh táchat hashámesh, “there is nothing new under the sun”) found in Ecclesiastes 1:9.

parole.significato: The world, a place where difficulties and the sorrows of life are felt, especially (Christianity) as a place to be left…
parole.testo: Calque of Latin lacrimārum vallis from the “Salve Regina” (a hymn to the Virgin Mary), based on Hebrew עמק הבכא (ʿēmeq habbāḵāʾ) from Psalm 84:6 of the Bible.
